title: Open the global search palette with the keyboard shortcut (K / Cmd+K)
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App.
2. You are on any page (for example the Work Orders list).
3. The persistent search field is visible in the app header and shows the shortcut hint 'Search Cmd+K'.
steps: 1. Without clicking anything, press K together with the Command key (Ctrl+K on Windows), as shown in the header search field.
expected: 1. A centered search box (a modal overlay) opens on top of the page.
2. The page behind the box is dimmed.
3. The search input is focused so you can type right away.
4. The placeholder reads 'Search or ask a question'.
5. The footer keyboard legend is visible: 'Navigate' with up/down arrows, 'Select' with the enter symbol, and 'Close esc'.
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.1 Trigger and Surface; 8 Functional Requirements
notes: Wording taken from design-notes (placeholder 'Search or ask a question'; footer legend). Footer legend order differs slightly between Figma captures and spec prose - VIU-confirm exact on-screen footer text once the feature is on a QA env.

title: Open the global search palette by clicking the header search field
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App.
2. The persistent search field is visible in the app header, showing 'Search Cmd+K'.
steps: 1. Click the search field in the app header.
expected: 1. The centered search box (modal overlay) opens, anchored to the header search field.
2. The page behind is dimmed.
3. The input is focused and shows the placeholder 'Search or ask a question'.
4. The footer keyboard legend is visible.
notes: Entry-point placement itself: the header component in design-notes screenshot 8 is labelled OUT OF SCOPE (proposed placement). Confirm the ACTUAL entry-point placement against the shipped build at VIU time.

title: Close the palette with the Esc key
preconditions: 1. The global search palette is open.
expected: 1. The search box closes.
2. The dimming is removed and you are back on the page you were on.
3. Keyboard focus returns to the page (or the header search field).
notes: Spec 5.5 requires focus management: focus trap while open, return-focus on close - VIU-confirm focus returns correctly.

title: Toggle the palette closed by pressing the shortcut again (Cmd+K)
preconditions: 1. The global search palette is open (you opened it with Cmd+K or by clicking the header field).
steps: 1. Press K together with the Command key (Ctrl+K on Windows) again.
expected: 1. The search box closes.
2. The dimming is removed and you are back on the page.
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.1 (Esc, clicking underlay, or Cmd+K again closes it)
notes: Cmd+K acts as a toggle (open when closed, close when open).

title: Close the palette by clicking the dimmed page behind it
preconditions: 1. The global search palette is open.
2. The page behind the box is dimmed.
steps: 1. Click anywhere on the dimmed area of the page (outside the search box).
expected: 1. The search box closes.
2. The dimming is removed and you are back on the page.
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.1 (clicking the page underlay closes it)

title: Move through result rows with the Up and Down arrow keys, skipping group headers
preconditions: 1. The palette is open and you have typed a query that returns results in more than one group (for example 'Fib' returning Work orders and Customers).
2. Results are grouped under headings such as 'Work orders (12)' and 'Customers (2)'.
steps: 1. Press the Down arrow key several times.
2. Then press the Up arrow key several times.
3. Watch which item is highlighted after each press.
expected: 1. Each Down press moves the highlight to the next result row.
2. Each Up press moves the highlight to the previous result row.
3. The highlight moves only across result rows - the group heading lines (for example 'Work orders (12)') are skipped and never get the highlight.
4. When moving down past the last row of one group, the highlight continues into the first row of the next group.
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.5 (Up/Down moves focus through visible rows, skipping group headers)

title: Open the highlighted result in the same tab by pressing Enter
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with results showing.
2. You have highlighted a result row using the arrow keys.
expected: 1. The palette closes and the highlighted record opens in the same browser tab.
2. You land on that record's page (for example the Work Order detail page).
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.5 (Enter opens the focused row in the same tab)

title: Open the highlighted result in a new browser tab with Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter)
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with results showing.
2. You have highlighted a result row using the arrow keys.
steps: 1. Press Enter together with the Command key (Ctrl+Enter on Windows).
2. Watch the screen and the browser tabs.
expected: 1. The highlighted record opens in a NEW browser tab.
2. The page you were on (and, per build behavior, the palette) remains in the original tab.
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.5 (Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter opens in a new browser tab)
notes: VIU-confirm whether the palette stays open in the original tab or closes.

title: Move focus to the scope tab strip with Tab, then cycle tabs with Left and Right arrows
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in.
2. The scope tab strip is visible under the input: All, Work Orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part Sales.
steps: 2. Press the Right arrow key a few times.
3. Press the Left arrow key a few times.
expected: 1. Pressing Tab moves keyboard focus onto the scope tab strip.
2. Each Right arrow press moves to the next tab to the right; each Left arrow press moves to the previous tab.
3. Selecting a tab scopes the results to that entity type.
4. Focus does not leave the palette (focus stays trapped inside the modal).
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.5 (Tab moves focus to the scope tab strip; Left/Right cycles tabs when focus is on the tab strip)

title: The keyboard shortcut legend stays visible in the footer at all times
preconditions: 1. The palette is open.
steps: 1. Look at the bottom of the search box in the empty state.
2. Type a query so results appear, then look at the bottom again.
3. Clear the query and look again.
expected: 1. The footer keyboard legend is visible in every state: 'Navigate' with up/down arrows, 'Select' with the enter symbol, and 'Close esc'.
2. The legend does not disappear when results are showing or when the input is empty.
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.1 (footer always shows the keyboard legend)
notes: Exact footer text/order differs between Figma captures ('Navigate up/down, Select enter, Close esc') and spec prose ('up/down Navigate, enter Select, Esc Close') - VIU-confirm exact on-screen wording. Label captured from design-notes.

title: The scope tab strip lists All plus the six entity tabs in the exact order
permissions_required: A user with access to all six entity types.
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in that returns results.
steps: 1. Read the horizontal tab strip directly under the search input, left to right.
expected: 1. The tabs read, in this exact left-to-right order: All, Work Orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part Sales.
2. The 'All' tab is selected by default.

title: The 'All' tab shows results from every entity group together
permissions_required: A user with access to all six entity types.
preconditions: 1. The palette is open.
2. Test data exists so a single query (for example 'Fib') matches Work Orders, Customers, Assets, Parts and Vendors.
steps: 1. Make sure the 'All' tab is selected.
expected: 1. Results from every matching entity type appear, each under its own group heading with a count (for example 'Work orders (12)', 'Customers (2)').
2. Groups appear in the order Work Orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part Sales.

title: The 'Work Orders' tab shows only Work Order results
permissions_required: A user with Work Orders access.
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in that matches more than one entity type.
expected: 1. Only Work Order results are shown; other entity groups (Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part Sales) are hidden.
2. The 'Work Orders' tab appears selected/active.
spec_ref: requirements.md 5.2 State 3 (selecting a tab scopes the query to that entity type)

title: The 'Customers' tab shows only Customer results
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in that matches more than one entity type.
expected: 1. Only Customer results are shown; other entity groups are hidden.
2. The 'Customers' tab appears selected/active.

title: The 'Assets' tab shows only Asset (vehicle) results
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in that matches more than one entity type.
expected: 1. Only Asset results are shown; other entity groups are hidden.
2. The 'Assets' tab appears selected/active.

title: The 'Parts' tab shows only Part (inventory) results
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in that matches more than one entity type.
expected: 1. Only Part results are shown; other entity groups are hidden.
2. The 'Parts' tab appears selected/active.

title: The 'Vendors' tab shows only Vendor results
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in that matches more than one entity type.
expected: 1. Only Vendor results are shown; other entity groups are hidden.
2. The 'Vendors' tab appears selected/active.

title: The 'Part Sales' tab shows only Part Sales results
permissions_required: A user with Part Sales access.
preconditions: 1. The palette is open with a query typed in that matches Part Sales records.
2. At least one Part Sale exists (for example 'P2-58').
expected: 1. Only Part Sales results are shown; other entity groups are hidden.
2. The 'Part Sales' tab appears selected/active.
spec_ref: requirements.md 4 (Part Sales is a NEW searchable entity); 5.2 State 3
notes: Part Sales is a brand-new searchable entity vs today's global search.
